Unlike with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f8SBoXiXQjlCKqly]{Illusory Creature} spell, creatures in your scene lack combat abilities and statistics. Your scene doesn't include changes to the environment around it, though you can place your scene within the illusory environment of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HBJPsonQnWcC3qdX]{Mirage} spell.

When you create the scene, you can choose to have it be static or follow a program. Though a static scene is stationary, it includes basic natural movement. For example, wind blowing on an illusory piece of paper would rustle it. A program can be up to 1 minute long and repeats when finished. For instance, you could create a scene of two orcs fighting each other, and the fight would go the same way for each repetition. If you create a loop, the two fighters end up in the same place at the start of the scene and at the end of it, but you can smooth the program so it's hard to tell when the loop ends and begins. Anyone observing the scene for more than a few minutes almost always notices it looping. You're unable to alter the program after you create the illusion.

Any creature that touches any part of the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. If they interact with a portion of the illusion, they disbelieve only that portion. They disbelieve the entire scene only on a critical success.

Heightened (6th) Creatures or objects in your scene can speak. You must speak the specific lines for each actor when creating your program. The spell disguises your voice for each actor.

Heightened (8th) As the 6th-rank version, and the duration is unlimited.

spell->Invoke Spirits (Echo of the Past).name: Invoke Spirits (Echo of the Past)
spell->Invoke Spirits (Echo of the Past).description:
Ragged apparitions of the dead rise to stalk the living. They deal 2d4 mental damage and 2d4 void damage to each living creature in the area, with a basic Will save. Additionally, creatures that critically fail the save are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

On subsequent rounds, the first time you Sustain the Spell each round, you can move the area up to 30 feet within the range of the spell. Living creatures in the new area must attempt saves with the same effects as above, except that critically failing doesn't make them flee.

Heightened (+2) The mental damage and void damage each increase by 1d4.

spell->Wall of Stone (Echo of the Past).name: Wall of Stone (Echo of the Past)
spell->Wall of Stone (Echo of the Past).description:
You shape a wall of solid stone. You create a 1-inch-thick wall of stone up to 120 feet long, and 20 feet high. You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically, so you can use it to form a bridge or set of stairs, for example. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 14, and 50 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. A destroyed section of the wall can be moved through, but the rubble created from it is difficult terrain.

Heightened (+2) The Hit Points of each section of the wall increase by 15.

spell->One with Stone.name: One with Stone
spell->One with Stone.description:
You can either transform into a stone or merge with stone. While transformed, you can't move or affect anything outside the stone, but you can cast spells as long as they don't require line of effect beyond the stone. You can Dismiss this spell.

  • Merge with Stone The spell's duration is 10 minutes. While casting the spell, you must touch a stone with enough volume to fit you and your possessions or the spell is disrupted. While merged, you can hear, but not see, what's going on outside the stone. If the stone takes damage while you're inside it, you're expelled from the stone and take 10d6 damage. Magic passage expels you without dealing damage. The spell ends if you're ever outside the stone.
  • Turn into a Stone The spell's duration is 8 hours. You become a Large stone. Perception checks don't reveal your true nature, but a successful Nature or Survival check against your spell DC reveals that you appear to be a stone that is strangely new to the area. While in this form, you can observe everything around you, using your normal senses. As a stone, your AC is 23, and only status bonuses, status penalties, circumstance bonuses, and circumstance penalties affect you. Any successes and critical successes you roll on Reflex saves are failures

spell->Daze.name: Daze
spell->Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

action->Antiques.name: Antiques
action->Antiques.description: Each primordial echo possesses a signature magical item. The echo of Ayrzul holds the Might of the Blistering Labyrinth, a +3 greater striking high-grade abysium morningstar. The echo of Sairazul wears Pellucid Mercy, a glittering crystal diadem that functions as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.aQEQkwuAabZG8wY1]{Sage's Lash}. The echo of Cernock carries Builder's Ingenuity, a +3 greater striking halberd carved from green crystal that also functions as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.a8YCTjKnXySKpU5C]{Major Staff of Earth}. The echo gains the benefits of its item as if wearing or holding it and can activate its abilities, but it doesn't wield the item in combat.

action->Bury.name: Bury
action->Bury.description: Any creature hit by the locus's ancient stone Strike is partially buried in a tide of earth and rock, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} ([[/act escape dc=38]]).

action->Echo the Past.name: Echo the Past
action->Echo the Past.description:
The primordial echo calls forth a remnant of the past civilization to impart a lesson or control the present. Using this ability again ends any previous manifestation. The primordial echo casts one of the following occult innate spells (DC 38) for the listed purpose.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate} The dominated creature takes on the role of a historical figure or someone in the social hierarchy (such as high priest) from the primordial echo's civilization.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Ucf8eynbZMfUucjE]{Illusory Scene} The scene reenacts a historical event from the primordial echo's civilization.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.hghGRzOSzEl4UXdS]{Invoke Spirits} The spirits are drawn from the primordial echo's memories of people from their civilization.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.kOa055FIrO9Smnya]{Wall of Stone} The primordial echo recreates the wall of a building from their civilization, complete with decorations.

Psychocybin Caps.name: Psychocybin Caps
Psychocybin Caps.description: The mushrooms release spores that cause hallucinations, allowing the fungi to feed off the victim's psychic energy.
Psychocybin Caps.disable: @Check[nature|dc:35] or @Check[survival|dc:35] to cut back the mushrooms without triggering the spores
Psychocybin Caps.reset: If a creature within 10 feet of psychocybin caps becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3}, the effect generates enough mental energy to allow the fungi to reset.

action->Spore Eruption.name: Spore Eruption
action->Spore Eruption.description:
Trigger A creature moves onto the catwalk, Flies within 10 feet of the mushrooms, or damages the mushrooms

Effect The triggering creature and all creatures within 10 feet of them are exposed to psychocybin spores.

action->Psychocybin Spores.name: Psychocybin Spores
action->Psychocybin Spores.description:
A creature that becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3} reacts by releasing anything they're carrying. If the creature is holding onto a ladder, they fall.

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:36|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:stunned]

Maximum Duration 4 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[(1d12+12)[mental]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[(2d12+12)[mental]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (1 round)

Stage 3 @Damage[(3d12+12)[mental]] damage and stunned 3 (1 round)

Puzzle Gate.name: Puzzle Gate
Puzzle Gate.description: This complicated lock requires solving five puzzles in quick succession.
Puzzle Gate.disable: @Check[athletics|dc:44] (master) to [[/act force-open]] the gate, @Check[crafting|dc:41] or @Check[thievery|dc:41] (expert) twice to dismantle the puzzle lock, or @Check[Games Lore|dc:34] (expert) or @Check[society|dc:36] (expert) five times to solve the puzzles
Puzzle Gate.reset: The hazard resets after 1 minute if even one puzzle remains unsolved. The hazard doesn't reset if the gate is destroyed.
Puzzle Gate.routine: The puzzle makes an electroshock Strike against two different creatures.

action->Defense Activated.name: Defense Activated
action->Defense Activated.description:
Trigger A creature damages the gate or fails to bypass the gate by any other means other than a Games Lore or Society check

Effect The hazard makes an electroshock Strike against the triggering creature. The hazard then rolls initiative.

strike-melee->Electroshock.name: Electroshock
strike-melee->Electroshock.description: On a critical hit, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 minute.

Radlight Cap.name: Radlight Cap
Radlight Cap.publicNotes:
The radlights caps that flourish in many parts of Nar-Voth look like softly glowing, halfling-sized toadstools: a relatively common sight in the Darklands. When radlight caps change color, however, their dangerous nature becomes evident. With each color change, the fungi gain a new set of stimuli that trigger their deadly spore clouds. While a field of blue mushrooms may have attacked noisy interlopers, when they shift to red they assault anyone who moves a muscle. Many Nar-Voth natives, even non-sentient ones, have learned the colors and corresponding behaviors that will see them safely through a field of radlight caps.

Red Light, Green Light

Ayindilar elves claim that they originally cultivated radlight caps as an advanced warning system against radiation, and that the fungus's other color changes are merely an unintended mutation. Regardless, their original function remains useful enough that the elves rarely eradicate growths of radlight caps. Rather, they teach this warning rhyme to those who must pass through a radlight forest:

Red light stop,
Yellow drop.
Green light rush,
Blue light hush.
Black for terror, black for flight,
For this way comes the sickness light.

action->Color Change.name: Color Change
action->Color Change.description:
At the start of each round, the radlight cap changes color, going in order from red to yellow to green to blue and back to red, provided the radlight cap is alive and isn't black. Multiple radlight caps encountered within 100 feet of each other synchronize their color changes, such that all caps are the same color at the same time.

At the start of each round, if a radlight cap is within 100 feet of an object or creature that emits radiation, the radlight cap's color changes to black. While black, the radlight cap loses its Radlight aura and can't take actions or reactions.

action->Radlight.name: Radlight
action->Radlight.description: 30 feet. The aura sheds dim light the same color as the radlight cap's current color (see Color Change).

action->Radlight Spores.name: Radlight Spores
action->Radlight Spores.description:
Trigger The radlight cap takes damage or meets the condition corresponding to its current color, as described below

Effect The radlight cap uses Radlight Spores.

  • Blue The radlight cap detects a sound louder than a whisper.

  • Green A non-fungus creature within 30 feet ends their turn without having moved at least 5 feet.

  • Red A non-fungus creature within 30 feet takes an attack, move, or manipulate action that the radlight cap can detect.

  • Yellow A non-fungus creature within 30 feet ends their turn without being @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

action->Radlight Spores.name: Radlight Spores
action->Radlight Spores.description:
The radlight cap releases a cloud of spores in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30]. The spores deal @Damage[2d10|options:area-damage,radlight-spores] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:24|basic] save) to all non-fungus creatures in the area. The type of damage dealt and an additional effect is determined by the radlight cap's current color.

  • Blue The spores deal mental damage. Creatures that fail their save can't breathe or speak for 1 round.

  • Green The spores deal force damage. Creatures that fail their save are pushed 10 feet away from the radlight cap.

  • Red The spores deal fire damage. Creatures that fail their save are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round.

  • Yellow The spores deal electricity damage. Creatures that fail their save are knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

action->Slow.name: Slow
action->Slow.description: A risen ydrei is permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} and can't use reactions.

action->Baleful Bite.name: Baleful Bite
action->Baleful Bite.description:
Requirements The risen ydrei has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}

Effect The risen ydrei makes a fangs Strike against the grabbed creature. If the Strike hits and inflicts damage, the creature is exposed to necrotic venom.

action->Impenetrable Scales.name: Impenetrable Scales
action->Impenetrable Scales.description:
Frequency once per minute

Requirements The risen ydrei has taken physical damage since the end of its last turn

Effect The risen ydrei's immortal essence infuses its scales, making it virtually impervious to further blows. Until the start of its next turn, the risen ydrei gains resistance 20 to physical damage.

action->Necrotic Venom.name: Necrotic Venom
action->Necrotic Venom.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:37|options:inflicts:enfeebled]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} and regains 10 fewer Hit Points from all sources of healing (1 round)

Stage 2 enfeebled 1 and regains 20 fewer Hit Points from all sources of healing (1 round)

action->Slithering Surge.name: Slithering Surge
action->Slithering Surge.description:
Frequency once per minute

Requirements The risen ydrei's previous action was a successful Strike, and it doesn't have a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}

Effect The risen ydrei is empowered by its immortal essence to momentarily transcend the limitations of its undead form, darting across the battlefield in a murderous blur. It immediately Strides up to 25 feet and makes another attack of the same type against a different creature. This Strike uses the same multiple attack penalty as the previous one, but it counts toward the risen ydrei's multiple attack penalty as usual.

Rockfall.name: Rockfall
Rockfall.description: Rubble from the damaged walls falls on creatures that move into the area.
Rockfall.disable: @Check[crafting|dc:33] (expert) or @Check[athletics|dc:37] (expert) to shore up the crumbling walls
Rockfall.stealth: (trained) to spot the weakened areas of the walls

action->Collapse.name: Collapse
action->Collapse.description:
Trigger A creature moves into the hazard's area.

Effect A nearby wall collapses on the creature, dealing @Damage[(6d10+27)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:inflicts:immobilized,inflicts:prone] save). On a failed save, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} until it [[/act escape dc=34]]{Escapes}. On a critical failure, the creature is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. The area then becomes difficult terrain.

action->Armor-Rending Bite.name: Armor-Rending Bite
action->Armor-Rending Bite.description: The ankhrav makes a mandibles Strike; if the Strike hits, the target's armor takes the damage and the acid damage bypasses the armor's Hardness.

action->Spray Acid.name: Spray Acid
action->Spray Acid.description: The sciardav spews acid in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30], dealing @Damage[6d6[acid],1d6[acid,persistent]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic|options:area-effect] save). It can't Spray Acid again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Spray Acid]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Armor-Rending Bite.name: Armor-Rending Bite
action->Armor-Rending Bite.description: The ankhrav makes a mandibles Strike; if the Strike hits, the target's armor takes the damage and the acid damage bypasses the armor's Hardness.

action->Frenzy Pheromone.name: Frenzy Pheromone
action->Frenzy Pheromone.description: The hive mother unleashes a pheromone that causes all other sciardavs within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:100] to become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} until the start of the hive mother's next turn, and they can use the extra action only for Burrow, Stride, or Strike actions. The hive mother can't unleash the pheromone again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge unleash the pheromone]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Spray Acid.name: Spray Acid
action->Spray Acid.description: The hive mother spews acid in a @Template[type:cone|distance:60], dealing @Damage[12d6[acid],2d6[acid,persistent]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:31|basic|options:area-effect] save). It can't Spray Acid again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Spray Acid]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Alchemical Weakness.name: Alchemical Weakness
action->Alchemical Weakness.description: The guardian's weakness to alchemical items not only applies to damage from alchemical items, but the guardian also takes 5 damage when splashed with non-damaging alchemical items or dosed with alchemical poisons, even if they're immune to their other effects.

action->Blighted Consumption.name: Blighted Consumption
action->Blighted Consumption.description:
Trigger A creature within 30 feet eats or drinks (including an alchemical item or potion)

Effect The food or drink burns like the caustic substances fed to the mummy before its death. If the creature fails a @Check[fortitude|dc:30|options:inflicts:sickened] save, they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} after they finish the consumption and can't reduce their sickened condition while within 30 feet of any mummy.

action->Choking Pain.name: Choking Pain
action->Choking Pain.description:
Requirements The mummy's last action was a successful fist Strike

Effect The mummy shares the pain of its dying moments with the target of that Strike. That creature takes @Damage[5d8[void]] damage with a @Check[will|dc:30|basic] save. If the creature critically fails the saving throw, it can't speak for 1 round, including to Cast a Spell.

Serpent's Gaze.name: Serpent's Gaze
Serpent's Gaze.description: The circle opens to reveal a slitted serpent's eye, which begins to spin in hypnotizing fashion.
Serpent's Gaze.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:29] (expert) to carefully cover the eye without triggering the hazard, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (5th rank; counteract DC 29) to counteract the magic
Serpent's Gaze.reset: The trap resets when the door is opened and closed.

action->Entrancing Eye.name: Entrancing Eye
action->Entrancing Eye.description:
Trigger A non-sekmin creature without Nuzial's sigil moves adjacent to the door

Effect The trap attempts to place a lingering hypnotic vision of the serpent's eye in the minds of all creatures within a @Template[type:cone|distance:15]. Creatures in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:30|options:area-effect,inflicts:dazzled] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes a –2 status penalty to Perception checks for 1 day. This effect can be counteracted with a 4th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.EfFMLVbmkBWmzoLF]{Clear Mind} spell.

Failure As success, and the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} on the first round of any encounter.

Critical Failure As failure, except the duration is 1 week.

Shivver.name: Shivver
Shivver.publicNotes:
In some Darklands cultures, prisoners are routinely fleshwarped into grotesque shapes at the whims of their cruel captors. These unfortunate victims are dubbed "shivvers" after the thrill of horror they elicit and as a nod to one of the more infamous Darklands prisons. Once ordinary humanoids, shivvers now sport wriggling tentacles, insectile mandibles, and other bizarre "improvements." The agony these modifications cause is enough to drive many shivvers into murderous rages.

It's often said that encountering a fleshwarp is evidence there's an even greater monster nearby: the cruel being that tortured the fleshwarp into its distorted form. The Darklands are home to many such monsters, both the fleshwarps and their creators.

Fugitives of the Shiv

While some prisons pride themselves on being inescapable, the wardens of the Shiv once routinely released their more "artistically" fleshwarped captives before their sentences were fully served. The wardens believed that the products of their cruel punishments would inspire fear and obedience throughout the Darklands.

action->Pain-Wracked Rage.name: Pain-Wracked Rage
action->Pain-Wracked Rage.description:
Frequency once per day

Trigger The shivver takes more than 20 damage from a single instance of damage

Effect The shivver is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of their next turn. They're then @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}, but while quickened their regeneration is deactivated, and they can use the extra action only to Strike.

action->Compression.name: Compression
action->Compression.description: A shivver can move through a gap at least 1 foot wide without @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeezing} and can Squeeze through a gap at least 6 inches wide. Narrow confines are not difficult terrain for a shivver.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The shivver deals an additional 2d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Sicklight Wisp.name: Sicklight Wisp
Sicklight Wisp.publicNotes:
The greenish pall that sicklight wisps cast over their surroundings causes creatures within it to sicken and die. Whereas the will-o'-wisps typically encountered on the surface feed on fear, sicklight wisps feast on the illness they spread, taking joy in robbing creatures of their vigor and health.

Though most commonly associated with the pit of Mobhad Leigh, sicklight wisps are occasionally encountered elsewhere in the Darklands. Wicked creatures sometimes employ the wisps to foil attempts at scrying on their subterranean lairs, as anyone who uses magic to spy upon a sicklight wisp risks having their mind irrevocably shattered.

Curse of the Infirm

In the Darklands, sicklight wisps are feared by both healers and the sick, because they're drawn to hospitals and other places of healing. Able to travel invisibly and evade scrying, the wisps slip into sickrooms, becoming briefly visible as they drain the remaining life from ailing victims. To protect against the wisps, some long-standing institutions of healing have taken to planting radlight caps around their facilities, since these otherwise dangerous mushrooms turn black in the presence of even an invisible sicklight wisp.

action->Deep Sight.name: Deep Sight
action->Deep Sight.description: The sicklight wisp can see into and through solid matter within the radius of its sicklight glow. Certain metals (such as lead) block this vision.

action->Magic Immunity.name: Magic Immunity
action->Magic Immunity.description: A sicklight wisp is immune to all spells except @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gKKqvLohtrSJj3BM]{Force Barrage}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Oj1PJBMQD9vuwCv7]{Quandary}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.0qaqksrGGDj74HXE]{Revealing Light}, and vitality spells.

action->Scrying Sickness.name: Scrying Sickness
action->Scrying Sickness.description: The wisp automatically tries to counteract all magical detection, revelation, and scrying effects used against any target or location within 50 feet of the wisp, using their @Check[stealth] modifier for the counteract modifier. On a success, the creature that attempted the magical detection is targeted by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.5BbU1V6wGSGbrmRD]{Never Mind} spell (@Check[will|dc:33|options:item:type:spell|traits:concentrate,curse,incapacitation,manipulate,mental]).

action->Feed on Sickness.name: Feed on Sickness
action->Feed on Sickness.description:
Frequency once per round

Requirements An enemy within 15 feet of the sicklight wisp is sickened

Effect The sicklight wisp feeds on the creature's illness. The creature takes @Damage[4d10[void]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:33|basic] save). The wisp regains @Damage[2d10[healing]] Hit Points, and if the sicklight wisp has Gone Dark, their sicklight glow reactivates.

action->Go Dark.name: Go Dark
action->Go Dark.description: The sicklight wisp deactivates their Sicklight Glow, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. They can end this effect with another use of this action. If the wisp makes a radioactive touch Strike while invisible, the tracing of green energy left behind lets any observer determine the wisp's location, making them only @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to all observers until the wisp moves.

action->Sickening Touch.name: Sickening Touch
action->Sickening Touch.description: A creature hit by the sicklight wisp's radioactive touch Strike or that ends its turn in the wisp's sicklight glow aura must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:33|options:inflicts:sickened] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). If the creature is already sickened, their sickened value instead increases by 1 (by 2 on a critical failure), to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 4}. If the creature reaches sickened 4, they can't reduce their sickened value until the effect is counteracted by a cleanse affliction spell or similar effect.

action->Sicklight Glow.name: Sicklight Glow
action->Sicklight Glow.description: 50 feet. A sicklight wisp, though naturally @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}, glows with a greenish illumination, casting dim light in the aura and making them visible. A creature that ends its turn within the aura is subjected to the wisp's sickening touch.

action->Instinctive Teleportation.name: Instinctive Teleportation
action->Instinctive Teleportation.description:
Trigger The thruneosaurus takes damage from a holy effect

Effect The thruneosaurus teleports to an open space within 60 feet it can see, along with any creatures it has swallowed whole.

action->Hellfire Blast.name: Hellfire Blast
action->Hellfire Blast.description:
The thruneosaurus channels sulfurous hellfire in one of three ways. The thruneosaurus chooses the effect, but it can't make the same choice in two consecutive rounds.

  • Blistering Sun (divine, fire, unholy) The thruneosaurus ignites an orb of hellfire between its horns that radiates heat in a @Template[emanation|distance:30], dealing @Damage[2d8[persistent,fire]] damage.
  • Choking Fumes (divine, poison, unholy) The thruneosaurus exhales a @Template[cone|distance:60] of sulfurous smoke that deals @Damage[6d8[poison]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:38|traits:divine,poison,unholy|basic|options:area-effect] save). Creatures that fail their saves are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.
  • Fiery Beam (divine, fire, unholy) A @Template[line|distance:120] of hellish flame erupts from the thruneosaurus's eyes, dealing @Damage[6d10[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:38|traits:divine,fire,unholy|basic|options:area-effect] save).

Slithering Snakes.name: Slithering Snakes
Slithering Snakes.description: A black, snake-shaped rune summons sinuous, shadowy serpents to grab and bite intruders throughout the room.
Slithering Snakes.disable: @Check[acrobatics|dc:31] (expert) to approach the desk without triggering the trap, followed by @Check[thievery|dc:33] (expert) to erase the rune; conversely, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (6th rank; counteract DC 31) to counteract the rune

action->Slither.name: Slither
action->Slither.description:
Trigger A creature moves within 10 feet of the desk

Effect The hazard rolls initiative. On its turn, shadowy snakes appear throughout the room, filling the area with the effect of a 6th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.xFp4EwVcYwSG336t]{Slither} spell (DC 34) for 1 minute.

Sorcerous Skull Swarm.name: Sorcerous Skull Swarm
Sorcerous Skull Swarm.publicNotes:
The act of creating a demilich sometimes goes horribly awry, leaving behind a shattered remnant of a once-mighty spellcaster constantly leaking eldritch energies. The ruined spirit animates a cloud of debased copies of itself, glittering with cracked crystals in crude imitation, and it hungers constantly for the magical energies denied it in its corrupted immortality.

Some of the spellcaster's personality remains in the swarm, albeit usually unnaturally split between the skulls. As a consequence, the skulls argue among themselves as warring parts of the personality clamor to be heard, resulting in the swarm's fractious, inconstant attitude.

A skull swarm is composed of reanimated masses of craniums and jawbones, forming a terrifying avalanche of undead fury. Most skull swarms are mindless, though some retain a vestige of wit, awareness, and even magical talents from life, culminating in a highly intelligent swarm mind.
Sorcerous Skull Swarm.saveDetails: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

spell->Spell Riposte.name: Spell Riposte
spell->Spell Riposte.description:
Trigger You're the target of a spell you're aware of.

You attempt to counteract the triggering spell. If the spell would be counteracted, it instead continues with the caster as a target instead of you. Spell riposte can't affect spells that aren't targeted (such as area spells).

spell->Truesight (Constant).name: Truesight (Constant)
spell->Truesight (Constant).description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

spell->Dispel Magic (At Will).name: Dispel Magic (At Will)
spell->Dispel Magic (At Will).description: You unravel the magic behind a spell or effect. Attempt a counteract check against the target. If you successfully counteract a magic item, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. This doesn't change the item's non-magical properties. If the target is an artifact or similar item, you automatically fail.
spell->Dispel Magic (At Will).target: 1 spell effect or unattended magic item

spell->Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
spell->Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

spell->Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
spell->Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.
spell->Telekinetic Hand.target: 1 unattended object of light Bulk or less

spell->Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
spell->Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Boneshard Burst.name: Boneshard Burst
action->Boneshard Burst.description: When a sorcerous skull swarm is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it erupts in an explosion of foul energy and bone fragments in a @Template[burst|distance:30], dealing @Damage[3d12[piercing],3d12[void]|options:area-damage] (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect] save).

action->Consume Spell.name: Consume Spell
action->Consume Spell.description:
Trigger The sorcerous skull swarm is targeted with a spell

Effect The swarm casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} to counteract the triggering spell. If it successfully counteracts the spell, it gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the rank of the counteracted spell that last for 1 minute.

action->Siphon Magic.name: Siphon Magic
action->Siphon Magic.description: The sorcerous skull swarm saps magic from nearby creatures. Any creature with the ability to cast spells (including innate spells) in the swarm's space takes @Damage[15d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:stupefied] save); on a failure, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3} on a critical failure).

action->Swarming Gnaw.name: Swarming Gnaw
action->Swarming Gnaw.description: Each enemy in the swarm's space takes @Damage[5d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect] save).

spell->Touch of Death.name: Touch of Death
spell->Touch of Death.description:
Make a melee unarmed Strike. If you hit and the target is alive, anytime during the duration, you can spend a single action, which has the auditory and concentrate traits, to speak a word of death that could instantly slay it. The target must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target survives, the spell ends, and the target is then temporarily immune for 24 hours.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} and takes @Damage[5*@item.level] damage, the spell ends, and the target is then temporarily immune for 24 hours.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3} and takes @Damage[10*@item.level] damage. The spell's duration continues, but the target is then temporarily immune for 24 hours against being killed by touch of death.

Critical Failure The target dies.

If you cast touch of death again, the effects of any touch of death you had previously cast end.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 10 on a failure, or 5 on a success.

spell->Wild Winds Stance.name: Wild Winds Stance
spell->Wild Winds Stance.description:
You take on the stance of the flowing winds, sending out waves of energy at a distance. You can make wind crash unarmed Strikes as ranged Strikes against targets within 30 feet. These deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, nonlethal, propulsive, and unarmed traits. Wind crash Strikes ignore @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} and all cover.

While in wild winds stance, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against ranged attacks.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feat-effects.Item.eeAlh6edygcZIz9c]{Stance: Wild Winds Stance}

spell->Qi Blast.name: Qi Blast
spell->Qi Blast.description:
You unleash your qi as a powerful blast that deals 2d6 force damage. If you use 2 actions to cast qi blast, increase the size of the cone to 30 feet and the damage to 3d6. If you use 3 actions to cast qi blast, increase the cone to 60 feet and the damage to 4d6. Each creature in the area must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is pushed 5 feet.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is pushed 10 feet.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6, or by 2d6 if you use 2 or 3 actions.

spell->Inner Upheaval.name: Inner Upheaval
spell->Inner Upheaval.description:
You focus your qi into devastating magical attacks. Make an unarmed Strike or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.Item.NLHHHiAcdnZ5ohc2]{Flurry of Blows} (this doesn't change the limit on using only one flourish per turn). You gain a +1 status bonus to your attack rolls with the Strikes, and the Strikes deal 1d6 extra damage. This damage can be any of the following types of your choice, chosen each time you Strike: force, spirit, vitality, or void.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.8olfnTmWh0GGPDqX]{Spell Effect: Inner Upheaval}

Heightened (+4) The extra damage increases by 1d6

action->(Ghost) Rejuvenation.name: (Ghost) Rejuvenation
action->(Ghost) Rejuvenation.description:
Setting right the injustice that led to Sourpuss's death allows him to move on to the afterlife.

When a ghost is destroyed, it re-forms after [[/br 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} within the location it's bound to, fully healed. A ghost can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting.

action->Disrupt Qi.name: Disrupt Qi
action->Disrupt Qi.description: Sourpuss attempts an unarmed Strike against a living creature. On a hit, the creature takes 3d6 persistent void damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} until the persistent damage ends.

action->Flurry of Blows.name: Flurry of Blows
action->Flurry of Blows.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect Sourpuss makes two fist Strikes. If both hit the same creature, combine their damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses.

action->Forbidden Palm.name: Forbidden Palm
action->Forbidden Palm.description:
Requirements The grandmaster has at least 1 Focus Point

Effect The grandmaster casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Ovvflf5aFbmBxqq8]{Touch of Death} (spending 1 Focus Point as normal). Any time the target attempts a Fortitude save against this touch of death, the grandmaster takes @Damage[40] damage and is permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1}. If the target gets a critical success, it's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}; if it gets a success or failure the stunned condition it gains is increased by 1, and any damage it takes is increased by 40.

action->One-Millimeter Punch.name: One-Millimeter Punch
action->One-Millimeter Punch.description:
2 or 3

The grandmaster makes a single, carefully controlled unarmed Strike that deals 2 additional dice of damage, or 4 additional dice if the grandmaster spent 3 actions. If this damages the target, the grandmaster can choose to make the target attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:38] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is pushed back 5 feet.

Failure The target is pushed back 10 feet.

Critical Failure The target is pushed back 10 feet for each action the grandmaster spent on One-Millimeter Punch.

action->Powerful Fists.name: Powerful Fists
action->Powerful Fists.description: Sourpuss's fist Strikes don't take penalties when making lethal attacks and are treated as adamantine, cold iron, and silver.

Strangleroot.name: Strangleroot
Strangleroot.publicNotes:
In the shallowest parts of the Darklands, roots sometimes break through cavern ceilings, dangling from above like living stalactites. The most deep-seated of these roots belong to carnivorous trees that draw sustenance not only from the soil, but from the blood of the creatures that wander beneath them. When people on the surface encounter a tree whose leaves are an out-of-season autumnal red, they're likely unaware that, somewhere deep underground, the tree's roots have snared a hapless Darklands creature and are draining its blood.

Darklands inhabitants who live beneath strangleroot forests learn to keep their eyes on the ceiling, where strangleroot taproots lurk. They also watch for desiccated corpses, either strewn about the floor or suspended from the ceiling by hanging roots.

Slow Digestion

Strangleroots might strike with lightning speed, but they have the patience of a slow-growing tree. Once they have a victim trussed up tight, they rarely drain all its blood at once; rather, they do so over the course of hours or days. They accelerate their feeding only to kill a troublesome captive or to engorge themselves, lacing their meal's blood with a poisonous sap as a deterrent against hostile creatures.

action->Blood Engorged.name: Blood Engorged
action->Blood Engorged.description: When the strangleroot is first encountered, it isn't usually blood engorged. When the strangleroot uses Drain Blood, it becomes blood engorged for 1 hour or until it uses Blood Spray, whichever comes first. While blood engorged, the strangleroot turns red and loses its immunity to bleed damage.

action->Blood Spray.name: Blood Spray
action->Blood Spray.description:
Requirements The strangleroot is blood engorged

Effect The strangleroot sprays sap-poisoned blood in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20]. Each creature in the emanation takes @Damage[6d10[poison]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:25|basic|options:area-effect] save. Afterward, the strangleroot is no longer blood engorged.

action->Drain Blood.name: Drain Blood
action->Drain Blood.description:
Requirements The strangleroot has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}

Effect The restrained creature takes @Damage[3d10[bleed]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. The strangleroot regains HP equal to the bleed damage dealt and becomes blood engorged. The strangleroot doesn't gain Hit Points from draining a creature that's already drained, but the creature's drained value increases by 1, killing them when they reach @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 5}. A creature's drained condition decreases by 1 per hour.

action->Haul Up.name: Haul Up
action->Haul Up.description:
Requirements The strangleroot has a Large or smaller creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}

Effect The creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save or it's pulled up to 15 feet upwards and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}.

action->Retract.name: Retract
action->Retract.description:
Requirements The strangleroot doesn't have a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}

Effect The strangleroot retracts its dangling roots into the ceiling or re-extends its roots. While retracted, the strangleroot can't be targeted by attacks or effects, and it can't take any action except to extend its roots, reappearing in another space within 15 feet of the space it left. If a creature digs through 1 foot of the earth and stone, it removed the earthen layer protecting the strangleroot; the strangleroot is no longer retracted and can't use Retract again.

Tajatizt.name: Tajatizt
Tajatizt.publicNotes:
To outsiders, the eldritch emeritus looks something like a joke—a befuddled old scholar, their mind so stuffed with obscure theorems and abstract metaphysics that concerns about mere daily reality fade away. Those who know them, however, know that the eldritch emeritus wrote more treatises of spells than most wizards have had hot dinners, and if sufficiently annoyed, is entirely capable of providing a brief, thorough, and fatal demonstration.

True power comes from knowledge—the power to shape the growth of kingdoms by mere whispers, stay three steps ahead of adversaries, or even know which flora is best for creating untraceable poisons.

spell->Detonate Magic.name: Detonate Magic
spell->Detonate Magic.description: You cause the magic within the target to dissipate in a destructive explosion. You attempt to counteract the target. If the attempt succeeds, an explosion of magical force deals 8d6 force damage with a basic Reflex save. If you successfully counteract the magic of an item, it's deactivated for 1 week (or destroyed on a critical success) and the explosion is a 5-foot emanation from the item. If you successfully counteract a spell, the effect ends and the explosion affects either all creatures in the spell's area or the target of the spell and all creatures in a 5-foot emanation around it.

spell->Falling Stars.name: Falling Stars
spell->Falling Stars.description:
Area 4 40-foot bursts

You reach into the skies and call down an array of falling stars that explode upon colliding with the ground. Choose for the falling stars to be airbursts (sonic), asteroids (fire), comets (cold), or plasma (electricity). The spell gains the trait of the falling star type you chose. The four stars' central 10-foot bursts can't overlap. Each falling star deals 6d10 bludgeoning damage to each creature in the @Template[burst|distance:10] at the center of its area of effect before exploding, dealing 14d6 energy damage of the type you chose to each creature in its @Template[burst|distance:40]. A creature in any of the areas attempts one basic Reflex save against the spell no matter how many overlapping explosions it's caught in and can take each type of damage only once.

Heightened (+1) The bludgeoning damage increases by 1d10, and the energy damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Earthquake.name: Earthquake
spell->Earthquake.description:
You shake the ground, topple creatures into fissures, and collapse structures. The GM might add additional effects in certain areas. Cliffs might collapse, causing creatures to fall, or a lake might drain as fissures open up below its surface, leaving a morass of quicksand.

  • Shaking Ground The ground is difficult terrain, and creatures on it take a -2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, AC, and skill checks. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.09rtx50laDw68FGT]{Spell Effect: Earthquake (Shaking Ground)}
  • Fissures Each creature on the ground must attempt a Reflex save at the start of its turn to keep its footing and avoid falling into 40-foot-deep fissures that open beneath it. The fissures are permanent, and their sides require successful @Check[athletics|dc:15|traits:action:climb] to Climb.
  • Collapse Structures and ceilings might collapse. The GM rolls a flat check for each (@Check[flat|dc:16] for a sturdy structure, @Check[flat|dc:14] for an average structure and most natural formations, @Check[flat|dc:9] for a shoddy structure, all adjusted higher or lower as the GM sees fit). A collapse deals 11d6 bludgeoning damage to each creature caught in it with a basic Reflex save. A creature falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} unless it critically succeeds and falls into a fissure if it critically fails.

Heightened (10th) You create a massive earthquake that can devastate a settlement. The range increases to half a mile and the area to a quarter-mile burst.

spell->Quandary.name: Quandary
spell->Quandary.description:
You transport the target into an extraplanar puzzle room of mysterious origin, locking them there. Once each turn as a single action, the target can attempt an @Check[occultism] check, @Check[perception] check, or @Check[thievery] check against your spell DC to solve the puzzle. Teleportation effects can't carry the target outside the puzzle room unless they can also traverse the planes, such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.5bTt2CvYHPvaR7QQ]{Interplanar Teleport}. When the spell ends, the target returns to the space it occupied when it was banished, or to the nearest space if the original is now filled.

Critical Success The target solves the puzzle and escapes.

Success The target is on the right path to the solution. If it was already on the right path, it solves the puzzle and escapes.

Failure The target makes no progress toward a solution.

Critical Failure The target makes no progress and, if it was on the right path, it no longer is.

spell->Energy Aegis (Constant).name: Energy Aegis (Constant)
spell->Energy Aegis (Constant).description:
You protect the target with a powerful, long-lasting energy barrier. The target gains resistance 5 to acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, sonic, vitality, and void damage.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.4Lo2qb5PmavSsLNk]{Spell Effect: Energy Aegis}

Heightened (9th) The resistances increase to 10.

spell->Project Image.name: Project Image
spell->Project Image.description:
You project an illusory image of yourself. You must stay within range of the image, and if at any point you can't see the image, the spell ends. Whenever you Cast a Spell other than one whose area is an emanation, you can cause the spell effect to originate from either yourself or the image. Because the image is an illusion, it can't benefit from spells, though visual manifestations of the spell appear. The image has the same AC and saves as you. If it is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends.

Heightened (+2) The maximum duration you can Sustain the spell increases to 10 minutes.

spell->Chain Lightning.name: Chain Lightning
spell->Chain Lightning.description:
You discharge a powerful bolt of lightning at the target, dealing 8d12 electricity damage. The target must attempt a basic Reflex save. The electricity arcs to another creature within 30 feet of the first target, jumps to another creature within 30 feet of that target, and so on. You can end the chain at any point. You can't target the same creature more than once, and you must have line of effect to all targets. Roll the damage only once, and apply it to each target (halving or doubling as appropriate for its saving throw outcome). The chain ends if any one of the targets critically succeeds at its save.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d12.
spell->Chain Lightning.target: 1 creature, plus any number of additional creatures

spell->Disintegrate.name: Disintegrate
spell->Disintegrate.description:
A black tracer bolt flies toward your target, and upon making contact intensifies into a powerful destructive beam. Make a spell attack against the target. If you hit an object or force construct (such as a wall of force), it's destroyed with no save unless it's an artifact or similarly powerful. A single casting can destroy no more than a 10-foot cube of matter. If you hit a creature, it takes 12d10 damage (no damage type) with a basic Fortitude save. If you critically hit, the target gets a result one degree of success worse than the outcome of its Fortitude save. A creature reduced to 0 HP is blasted to fine powder; its gear remains.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d10.
spell->Disintegrate.target: 1 creature, unattended object, or force construct

spell->Teleport.name: Teleport
spell->Teleport.description:
You and the targets are instantly transported to any location within range, as long as you can identify the location precisely both by its position relative to your starting position and by its appearance (or other identifying features). Incorrect knowledge of the location's appearance usually causes the spell to fail, but it could instead lead to teleporting to an unwanted location or some other unusual mishap determined by the GM. Teleport is not precise over great distances. The targets appear at a distance from the intended destination equal to roughly 1 percent of the total distance traveled, in a direction determined by the GM. For short journeys, this lack of precision is irrelevant, but for long distances this could be up to 1 mile.

Heightened (7th) You and the other targets can travel to any location within 1,000 miles.

Heightened (8th) You and the other targets can travel to any location on the same planet. If you travel more than 1,000 miles, you arrive only 10 miles off target.

Heightened (9th) You and the other targets can travel to any location on another planet within the same solar system. Assuming you have accurate knowledge of the location's position and appearance, you arrive on the new planet 100 miles off target.

Heightened (10th) As the 9th-rank version, but you and the other targets can travel to any planet within the same galaxy.
spell->Teleport.target: you and up to 4 targets touched, either willing creatures or objects roughly the size of a creature.

spell->Wall of Force.name: Wall of Force
spell->Wall of Force.description:
You form an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} wall of pure magical force up to 50 feet long and up to 20 feet high. The wall has no discernible thickness. You must create the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost. The wall has AC 10, Hardness 30, and 60 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. The wall blocks physical effects from passing through it, and because it's made of force, it blocks incorporeal and ethereal creatures as well. Teleportation effects can pass through the barrier, as can visual effects (since the wall is invisible). Wall of force is immune to counteracting effects of its level or lower, but the wall is automatically destroyed by a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.r7ihOgKv19eJQnik]{Disintegrate} spell of any rank.

Heightened (+2) The Hit Points of the wall increase by 20.

spell->Banishment.name: Banishment
spell->Banishment.description:
You send the target back to its home plane. The target must attempt a Will save. You can spend an extra action while Casting this Spell and add a cost to the spell to give the creature a –2 circumstance penalty to its save. The cost must be a specially gathered object that is anathema to the creature. This spell fails if you aren't on your home plane when you cast it.

Critical Success The target resists being banished and you are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Success The target resists being banished.

Failure The target is banished.

Critical Failure The target is banished and can't return by any means to the plane it's banished from for 1 week.

Heightened (9th) You can target up to 10 creatures. The extra cost affects targets to which it is anathema.
spell->Banishment.target: 1 creature that isn't on its home plane

spell->Howling Blizzard.name: Howling Blizzard
spell->Howling Blizzard.description:
Freezing winds extend from your hands, pushing away from you with great force. If you Cast this Spell with 2 actions, it has an area of a 60-foot cone; if you Cast this Spell with 3 actions, it has a range of 500 feet and an area of a 30-foot burst. Each creature in the area takes 10d6 cold damage with a basic Reflex save. Snowdrifts and icy gales fill the area until the start of your next turn, making the area difficult terrain.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Slither.name: Slither
spell->Slither.description:
A mass of snakes made of shadow rise up to capture creatures in the area. Each creature in the area when you Cast the Spell takes 3d6 piercing damage and 1d6 persistent poison damage from a biting snake, and it's grabbed or restrained depending on its Reflex save. A creature that ends its turn in the area must also attempt this save, even if it's already grabbed or restrained by the snakes. You can Dismiss the spell.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by a snake. The snakes' [[/act escape]] DC is equal to your spell DC. A creature can attack a snake to release the creature. A snake's AC is equal to your spell DC, and it's destroyed if it takes 12 or more damage at once. New snakes continually regrow as long as the spell lasts, so destroying snakes doesn't prevent slither from capturing more creatures.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by a snake.

Heightened (+2) The persistent poison damage increases by 1d6 and snake HP increases by 6.

spell->Creation.name: Creation
spell->Creation.description:
You conjure a temporary object from magical energy. It must consist of earthen or plant-derived matter (such as wood, paper, brick, or stone) and be 5 cubic feet or smaller. It can't rely on intricate artistry or complex moving parts, never fulfills a cost or the like, and can't be made of precious materials or materials with a rarity of uncommon or higher. It is obviously temporarily conjured, and thus can't be sold or passed off as a genuine item. The spell gains the appropriate trait for the item created, typically earth, plant, or wood.

Heightened (5th) The item is metal and can include common minerals, like feldspar or quartz. The spell gains the metal trait if used to create a metal object

spell->Fly.name: Fly
spell->Fly.description:
The target can soar through the air, gaining a fly Speed equal to its Speed or 20 feet, whichever is greater.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.MuRBCiZn5IKeaoxi]{Spell Effect: Fly}

Heightened (7th) The duration increases to 1 hour.

spell->Earthbind.name: Earthbind
spell->Earthbind.description:
Using the weight of earth, you hamper a target's flight, with effects based on its Fortitude save. If the creature reaches the ground safely, it doesn't take falling damage.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target falls safely up to 120 feet.

Failure The target falls safely up to 120 feet. If it hits the ground, it can't Fly, levitate, or otherwise leave the ground for 1 round.

Critical Failure The target falls safely up to 120 feet. If it hits the ground, it can't Fly, levitate, or otherwise leave the ground for 1 minute.

spell->Haste.name: Haste
spell->Haste.description:
Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.ElkXovNrHB0Doi6O]{Spell Effect: Haste}

spell->Locate.name: Locate
spell->Locate.description:
You learn the direction to the target (if you picked a specific object, such as "my mother's sword") or the nearest target (if you picked a type of object, such as "swords"). If the target is a specific object, you must have observed it directly with your own senses. If it's a type of object, you still need to have an accurate mental image of the type of object. If there's lead or running water between you and the target, this spell can't locate the object. This means you might find a type of object farther away if the nearest one is behind lead or running water.

Heightened (5th) You can target a specific creature or ancestry instead of an object, but you must have met or seen up close the creature or ancestry you want to target.
spell->Locate.target: 1 specific object or type of object

spell->Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
spell->Dispel Magic.description: You unravel the magic behind a spell or effect. Attempt a counteract check against the target. If you successfully counteract a magic item, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. This doesn't change the item's non-magical properties. If the target is an artifact or similar item, you automatically fail.
spell->Dispel Magic.target: 1 spell effect or unattended magic item

spell->Gecko Grip.name: Gecko Grip
spell->Gecko Grip.description:
Tiny clinging hairs sprout across the creature's hands and feet, offering purchase on nearly any surface. The target gains a climb Speed equal to its Speed.

Heightened (5th) The duration increases to 1 hour.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.qn7uO5Ih01yLJot7]{Spell Effect: Gecko Grip}

spell->Translate.name: Translate
spell->Translate.description:
The target can understand the meaning of a single language it is hearing or reading when you cast the spell. This doesn't let it understand codes, language couched in metaphor, and the like (subject to GM discretion). If the target can hear multiple languages and knows that, it can choose which language to understand; otherwise, choose one of the languages randomly.

Heightened (3rd) The target can also speak the language.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 creatures, and targets can also speak the language.

spell->Water Walk.name: Water Walk
spell->Water Walk.description:
The target can walk on the surface of water and other liquids without falling through. It can go underwater if it wishes, but in that case it must Swim normally. This spell doesn't grant the ability to breathe underwater.

Heightened (4th) The spell's range increases to 30 feet, the duration increases to 1 hour, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
spell->Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.bikFUFRLwfdvX2x2]{Invisibility Potion}) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

spell->Fleet Step.name: Fleet Step
spell->Fleet Step.description:
You gain a +30-foot status bonus to your Speed.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.ThFug45WHkQQXcoF]{Spell Effect: Fleet Step}

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

spell->Sigil.name: Sigil
spell->Sigil.description:
You harmlessly place your unique magical sigil, which is about 1 square inch in size, on the targeted creature or object. The mark can be visible or invisible, and you can change it from one state to another by using an Interact action to touch the target. The mark can be scrubbed or scraped off with 5 minutes of work. If it's on a creature, it fades naturally over the course of a week. The time before the mark fades increases depending on your heightened rank.

Heightened (3rd) The sigil instead fades after 1 month.

Heightened (5th) The sigil instead fades after 1 year.

Heightened (7th) The sigil never fades.

spell->Sure Strike.name: Sure Strike
spell->Sure Strike.description:
The next time you make an attack roll before the end of your turn, roll it twice and use the better result. The attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the target being @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}. You are then temporarily immune to sure strike for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.fpGDAz2v5PG0zUSl]{Spell Effect: Sure Strike}

spell->Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
spell->Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.
spell->Telekinetic Hand.target: 1 unattended object of light Bulk or less

weapon->+2 Greater Striking Staff of Fir.name: +2 Greater Striking Staff of Fire (Major)
weapon->+2 Greater Striking Staff of Fir.description:
This staff resembles a blackened and burned length of ashen wood. You can Interact to touch the tip of this staff to a torch, tinder, or a flammable substance to ignite a flame.

Activate Cast a Spell

Effect You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.

  • Cantrip @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6DfLZBl8wKIV03Iq]{Ignition}
  • 1st @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.y6rAdMK6EFlV6U0t]{Breathe Fire}
  • 2nd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.y6rAdMK6EFlV6U0t]{Breathe Fire}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2ZdHjnpEQJuqOYSG]{Floating Flame}
  • 3rd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2ZdHjnpEQJuqOYSG]{Floating Flame}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball}
  • 4th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.YrzBLPLd3r9m6t1p]{Fire Shield}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball} @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IarZrgCeaiUqOuRu]{Wall of Fire}
  • 5th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball} @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IarZrgCeaiUqOuRu]{Wall of Fire}

Craft Requirements Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.

equipment->Somewhat Disheveled Accolade.name: Somewhat Disheveled Accolade Robe
equipment->Somewhat Disheveled Accolade.description:
Although not all wizards have gone through formal training, it's become tradition to enchant robes representing the arduous training required and festoon them with honors one has earned. Typically, an accolade robe is styled after a single wizard school, with appropriate colors and symbols. Wearing these robes grants a +2 item bonus to Arcana checks.

The pockets of the robe tie to an extradimensional space that can hold 1 Bulk of items, none of which can have greater than light Bulk. The items must be related to spellcasting and academics—spellbooks, scrolls, wands, scholarly journals, and other academic supplies the GM allows. These items do not count against your Bulk limit. You can Interact to retrieve or stow items normally.

Activate—Review 1 (concentrate, manipulate)

Effect You retrieve an item of your choice from the robe's storage, then Recall Knowledge.

Activate—Extra Credit F (concentrate)

Frequency once per day

Effect You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a school spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it is lost.

Craft Requirements You are a wizard of the associated school.

equipment->Spellbook.name: Spellbook
equipment->Spellbook.description: A spellbook holds the written knowledge necessary to learn and prepare various spells, a necessity for wizards (who typically get one for free) and a useful luxury for other spellcasters looking to learn additional spells. Each spellbook can hold up to 100 spells. The Price listed is for a blank spellbook.

effect->Spell Effect: Energy Aegis.name: Spell Effect: Energy Aegis
effect->Spell Effect: Energy Aegis.description:
Granted by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.m2xFMNyQiUKQDRaj]{Energy Aegis}

The target gains resistance to acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, sonic, vitality, and void damage.

action->Counterspell.name: Counterspell
action->Counterspell.description:
Trigger A creature casts a spell the eldritch emeritus has prepared.

Effect The emeritus expends a prepared spell to counter the triggering creature's casting of that same spell. The emeritus loses their spell slot as if they had cast the triggering spell. The emeritus then attempts to counteract the triggering spell.

action->Third Contingent Sequencer.name: Third Contingent Sequencer
action->Third Contingent Sequencer.description:
Frequency once per day

Trigger A creature attacks or uses a spell or ability that would affect the eldritch emeritus

Effect A masterpiece of complex spellwork instantly takes shape, casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.YrzBLPLd3r9m6t1p]{Fire Shield}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WPXzPl7YbMEIGWfi]{Mislead}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2BV2yYPfVJ5zirZt]{Mountain Resilience} on the eldritch emeritus, each as an 8th-rank arcane spell.

action->Didactic Arcanism.name: Didactic Arcanism
action->Didactic Arcanism.description:
1 to 3

Requirements The eldritch emeritus has seen a creature Cast a Spell of 7th rank or lower during the previous round, that spell takes between one and three actions to cast, and that spell is on the arcane spell list

Effect The eldritch emeritus mastered that spell 30 years ago, and is happy to show how a real master does it. The emeritus Casts the same Spell but heightened to 8th rank. Didactic Arcanism uses the same number of actions as the original spell took to cast.

action->Steady Spellcasting.name: Steady Spellcasting
action->Steady Spellcasting.description: If a reaction would disrupt the eldritch emeritus's spellcasting action, the eldritch emeritus attempts a @Check[flat|dc:15]. On a success, the action isn't disrupted

Telepathic Whispers.name: Telepathic Whispers
Telepathic Whispers.description: The spirits of the dead entice visitors with forbidden knowledge.
Telepathic Whispers.disable: @Check[occultism|dc:40] or @Check[religion|dc:40] (expert) to ward off the spirits' influence, @Check[intimidation|dc:42] (trained) to silence the whispers. A PC who brandishes the gaze of eternity gains a +2 item bonus to their checks. Three successes total are required to disable the haunt.
Telepathic Whispers.reset: The hazard deactivates after 1 minute or after the spirits have answered three questions, whichever comes first. It resets after 24 hours.
Telepathic Whispers.routine: (1 action) The spirits peer into the minds of up to three creatures in the area. Each creature attempts a @Check[will|dc:40|options:area-effect,damaging-effect] save. On a failure, the target must choose to either divulge a closely guarded secret or take @Damage[(4d8+18)[mental]|options:area-damage] damage. On a critical success, the target can ask the haunt a question, which the spirits answer truthfully to the best of their ability.

action->Answer.name: Answer
action->Answer.description:
Trigger A creature enters the chamber

Effect The spirits whisper in a chorus of sibilant voices. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[(3d12+18)[mental]|options:area-damage] damage, with a @Check[will|dc:42|basic|options:area-effect] save. A creature that doesn't understand Sakvroth gains a +4 circumstance bonus to their save. The hazard then rolls initiative.

spell->Divine Decree.name: Divine Decree
spell->Divine Decree.description:
You utter a potent litany from your faith, a mandate that harms those who oppose your ideals. You deal 7d10 spirit damage to your enemies in the area; each enemy must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is enfeebled 2 for 1 minute. If you're on your home plane and the creature is not, the creature is sent back to its home plane. A creature of 10th level or lower must also succeed at a @Check[will|options:inflicts:paralyzed] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 minute; if it critically fails, it dies (this is a death effect).

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10, and the level of creatures that must attempt a second save on a critical failure increases by 2.

spell->Eclipse Burst.name: Eclipse Burst
spell->Eclipse Burst.description:
A globe of freezing darkness explodes in the area, dealing 8d10 cold damage to creatures in the area, plus an additional 8d4 void damage to living creatures. Each creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save.

If the globe overlaps with an area of magical light or affects a creature affected by magical light, eclipse burst attempts to counteract the light effect.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} by the darkness for an unlimited duration.

Heightened (+1) The cold damage increases by 1d10 and the void damage against the living increases by 1d4.

spell->Mask of Terror.name: Mask of Terror
spell->Mask of Terror.description:
The target appears to be a gruesome and terrifying creature. The effect is unique to each observer, so a human viewing the target might see a demon with bloody fangs, but a demon observing the target might see a glowing angelic visage.

When any creature attempts a hostile action against the target, the creature must attempt a Will save. It is then temporarily immune until the end of its next turn.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} before using its action.

Critical Failure The creature becomes frightened 2, and its action fails and is wasted.

Heightened (8th) You can target up to 5 creatures. If a creature uses a hostile action or reaction that affects multiple targets simultaneously, it needs to attempt only one save against mask of terror.

spell->Dominate.name: Dominate
spell->Dominate.description:
You take command of the target, forcing it to obey your orders. If you issue an obviously self-destructive order, the target doesn't act until you issue a new order. The effect depends on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} as it fights off your commands.

Failure You control the target. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlled} condition, but it can attempt a Will save at the end of each of its turns. On a success, the spell ends.

Critical Failure As a failure, but the target receives a new save only if you give it a new order that is against its nature, such as killing its allies.

Heightened (10th) The duration is unlimited.

spell->Truesight.name: Truesight
spell->Truesight.description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

spell->Vampiric Exsanguination.name: Vampiric Exsanguination
spell->Vampiric Exsanguination.description:
